summary: A listed company cannot make big changes to its non-convertible debt securities or preference shares without getting permission first. To get this permission from the stock exchange, the company must first get approval from its board, the debenture trustee, and most of its security holders. The company must also provide an online voting option to help gather this consent.
points: Must not make material modifications to the structure of non-convertible debt securities without prior approval from the stock exchange.
Must not make material modifications to the structure of non-convertible redeemable preference shares without prior approval from the stock exchange.
Must get approval from the board of directors before seeking stock exchange approval.
Must get approval from the debenture trustee before seeking stock exchange approval.
Must obtain written consent from the holders of at least three-fourths of the value of that class of securities.
Must provide the facility of remote e-voting to help security holders give their consent.
example: Sunrise Steel Limited has listed its non-convertible debt securities on the stock exchange. The company wants to make a material modification to the redemption structure of these securities. Before doing this, Sunrise Steel Limited must get the approval of its board of directors and the debenture trustee. It also needs to get written consent from holders representing at least three-fourths of the value of that class of securities. To collect this consent, the company provides a remote e-voting facility for the security holders. Only after completing these steps and obtaining the prior approval of the stock exchange can the company proceed with the modification.

terms.meaning: A significant or important change to something.
An entity that looks after the interests of the people who hold the debt securities.
A way for people to cast their votes online from a distance.

watch: Do not assume you can make changes just by getting board approval, as majority security holder consent and stock exchange approval are also required.
